title: Ectopic Expression of Human Thymosin β4 Confers Resistance to Legionella pneumophila during Pulmonary and Systemic Infection in Mice

what_it_measured.text: In order to test the function of Tb4 as a systemic anti-inﬂammatory agent, we investigated whether Tb4-Tg mice could be protected from L. pneumophila- FIG 5 Wild-type and Tb4-Tg macrophages were infected with L. pneumophila or stimulated with tlr2, tlr4, tlr5, and tlr9 ligands (CL419, LPS, ﬂagellin, and CpG).
Given that macrophages provide an intracellular habitat for L. pneumophila, we investigated which TLRs are stimulated during L. pneumophila infection.

endpoint.text: The deposition counts of L. pneumophila at t = 0 were measured from the lung samples harvested at 2 h following intranasal inoculation.
surviving bacterial CFU was measured at 0, 3, and 7 days after infection, and inﬁltrated immune cells were determined at 3 days postinfection.
To this end, we measured the production of inﬂammatory cytokines in WT and T b 4 macrophages after treatment with various TLR ligands in vitro.

reported_results.text: The CFU counts of surviving L. pneumophila in the WT and T b 4-Tg mice were compared by pooling the results from two different sets of infection experiments (n = 4 mice/group 1, n = 3 mice/group 2).
(B) Immunohistochemistry results of lungs from WT and T b 4-Tg mice at 3 and 7 days after nasal inoculation of 1 × 10⁹ L. pneumophila (n = 4 mice/group).

The data show mean values and standard deviations (SD) obtained from ﬁve mice (n = 5 mice/group). **, P , 0.01 and ***, P , 0.001 were considered signiﬁcant (one-way ANOVA followed by pairwise Tukey test).

As shown in Fig. 4A, T b 4-Tg BAL ﬂuid killed approximately 30% more L. pneumophila in vitro compared to the corresponding WT ﬂuid within 4 h, suggesting that human T b 4 is actively secreted into the airway lumen of transgenic mice and is likely to mediate in vitro killing of L. pneumophila by T b 4-Tg BAL ﬂuid.
